name: skye-open-source-spectacle-recipes
purpose: Concrete open-source frontend recipes agents must pull when the user asks for advanced effects. These recipes are not SkyeSol styling; they are implementation primitives.
rule: Pick recipes by behavior first, then apply brand taste. Do not make everything look like SkyeSol. Reading this file or calling audits is not implementation: selected recipes must be installed/imported/used in the target app source unless the user explicitly narrows scope.

imports: import { motion, useMotionValue, useSpring, useScroll, useTransform } from 'framer-motion';
recipes.useWhen: The page needs premium UI interaction, cursor-responsive layers, spring movement, layout transitions, or scroll-bound transforms.
avoid: static CSS pretending to be Framer Motion
recipes.starter: Use motion components for CTA/surface panels; use useMotionValue/useSpring for cursor glow; use useScroll/useTransform for scroll-bound depth.

recipes.useWhen: The first viewport needs a living object, shader field, spatial product symbol, particle system, or interactive canvas.
avoid: flat CSS glow sold as Three.js
recipes.starter: Build one dominant product object or shader field; bind camera/object motion to pointer and time.

recipes.useWhen: A Three/R3F scene needs cinematic lighting, depth, bloom, floating objects, stars, camera helpers, or visual finish.
recipes.starter: Wrap the scene with EffectComposer, add Bloom/Vignette, use Float/Stars/PerspectiveCamera to make the visual feel staged.

recipes.useWhen: The page needs a scroll-led story, sticky/pinned sections, scrubbed transitions, rails, staged proof, or cinematic funnel.
avoid: basic anchor scroll presented as GSAP
recipes.starter: Create Lenis raf loop, bind ScrollTrigger.update, and stage sections with scrubbed opacity/position/progress rails.

recipes.useWhen: A 3D scene or hero needs director-like keyframed parameters, camera beats, or reusable art-directed states.
mustShow: Theatre project/sheet or documented reason not to load studio in production
avoid: shipping studio UI to buyers by accident
recipes.starter: Use getProject for scene state; wire sheet values to camera, light, object rotation, or section beats.

imports: Use generated screenshot assets from browser QA; render them as first-class product media.
recipes.useWhen: The user has an app, dashboard, website, game, or tool where the real surface matters.
mustShow: caption proving what surface is shown
avoid: fake UI if real UI exists
recipes.starter: Capture real surfaces with Playwright, place them in an angled/staged gallery or first viewport subject.

imports: Use Playwright recordVideo or dense browser-action frames, encode with ffmpeg, render with <video autoplay muted loop playsinline>.
recipes.useWhen: The user asks for actual screenshots to become animated proof, or the page claims the app performs a workflow.
mustShow: video first in the proof stage
browser check that video is visible and playing
avoid: static landing screenshots called workflow proof
headline-first hero when actual surface proof was requested
recipes.starter: Use Playwright to goto/click/fill/scroll/submit through the claimed flow, record video or dense frames, encode H.264 with -movflags +faststart, render MP4/WebM, then verify readyState/currentTime/paused/visible in browser E2E.

packages: vanilla canvas or Three.js/OGL when selected
imports: Use the skyesol-living-background pattern pack for vanilla pages, or adapt the same behavior into Three/OGL when the target app already uses WebGL.
recipes.useWhen: The user asks for Skyes/SOL backgrounds that feel alive, moving command fields, aurora particles, living OS ambience, or pages that should not look like static gradients.
avoid: decorative orbs pretending to be motion
recipes.starter: Pull design_pattern_pack({ patternId: 'skyesol-living-background' }). Mount the canvas once at body level, keep it behind content, cap DPR to 2 or below, reduce particles on compact screens, and verify it is visible but not covering text.

imports: Call design_logo_manifest before drawing or generating any mark.
recipes.useWhen: Any page has a logo, brand mark, wordmark, favicon, nav identity, or product mark.
mustShow: transparent/floating placement when the asset supports it
clean wordmark fallback when no asset exists
avoid: replacing finished logos with generic initials
recipes.starter: Use the approved logo asset path from design_logo_manifest. If there is no exact asset, use typography-only wordmark plus parent brand endorsement rather than inventing a permanent emblem.

imports: Pull design_pattern_pack({ patternId: 'adaptive-neon-scrollbar' }), include both CSS and JS, and add data-mcp-neon-scrollbar to the root or scroll container that should opt in.
recipes.useWhen: The user explicitly asks for a visible neon/custom scrollbar, a scroll-led surface needs persistent position affordance, or a long horizontal rail/table needs branded scroll feedback.
mustShow: theme tokens or local brand variables
avoid: forcing the scrollbar on unrelated sites
cursor trail dependency when only scrollbar was requested
recipes.starter: Use the adaptive-neon-scrollbar pattern pack. Scope native styling with data-mcp-neon-scrollbar unless the target site explicitly wants global browser chrome. Include the JS rail updater so the user still sees the neon position rails when the OS/browser auto-hides native scrollbars. Map --mcp-neon-scrollbar-a/b/c/d to the local brand palette.

recipes.useWhen: The user asks for visible scrollbar, neon UI chrome, cursor trail, or tactile premium interaction.
avoid: thin invisible scrollbar on scroll-led pages
recipes.starter: Use CSS scrollbar thumb/track styling with a visible rgba track, neon gradient thumb, glow box-shadow, and a fixed pointer-events-none Framer Motion glow following pointer spring values.

imports: import { motion, useMotionValue, useScroll, useSpring, useTransform } from 'framer-motion';
recipes.useWhen: The page needs the Legal Skyes neon scrollbar plus stronger full-page motion polish: top scroll progress, pointer-reactive glow, animated scanline, shimmer display type, and magnetic hover utilities.
mustShow: scroll progress rail bound to useScroll
desktop cursor glow with pointer-events none
avoid: global motion with no reduced-motion escape
using chrome to hide a weak layout
recipes.starter: Use the neon-motion-chrome pattern pack. Wrap the page once, put .neon-gradient-text only on the hero/display line, use .neon-glow-panel for one or two proof surfaces, and add .neon-magnetic only to real controls.

recipes.useWhen: A product page needs real vector motion assets, loading states, illustrated workflows, or lightweight branded animations instead of CSS pretending to be media.
mustShow: loop/autoplay only when it supports the story
size constrained so it does not dominate the layout
avoid: large looping animations beside dense forms
autoplay animation with no reduced-motion fallback
recipes.starter: Use dotLottie for focused workflow/brand motion. Keep hero motion short, test mobile playback, and freeze or replace with a poster under prefers-reduced-motion.

recipes.useWhen: The page has a real .riv file and needs interactive vector animation: state-machine icons, product diagrams, animated controls, or brand characters.
mustShow: state machine or explicit playback control
avoid: inventing a Rive dependency without a .riv asset
using Rive for simple hover effects that CSS or Motion can handle
unbounded animation beside forms or dense UI
recipes.starter: Use Rive only when the asset exists. Wire state machine inputs to real page state or pointer interactions and provide a still fallback.

imports: import { Renderer, Program, Mesh, Triangle } from 'ogl';
recipes.useWhen: A lightweight shader field or custom WebGL backdrop is enough and React Three would be heavier than needed.
mustShow: animation loop paused or reduced under prefers-reduced-motion
avoid: shader backdrop hiding the product subject
calling it Three.js when it is OGL
recipes.starter: Use OGL for one restrained shader plane behind the main subject. Cap DPR near 1.25, pause on visibilitychange, and keep text readability clean.

recipes.useWhen: The design needs many 2D sprites, particles, game-like UI, or canvas interactions where DOM and Three are the wrong tool.
recipes.starter: Use Pixi for sprite-heavy or game-like motion only. Cap resolution, lower particle counts on compact screens, and keep DOM UI accessible above the canvas.

packages: copy source into project, then own and simplify it
imports: Audit copied snippets for accessibility, reduced-motion, bundle size, and local design fit before shipping.
recipes.useWhen: A designer/developer needs free component ideas for text effects, background motion, buttons, tabs, loaders, progress, or interactive blocks.
mustShow: adapted source rather than iframe/embed dependency
avoid: copying five unrelated effects into one viewport
shipping external demo code without accessibility review
using inspiration components instead of product-specific UX
recipes.starter: Pull one component idea, rewrite names/tokens to the local design system, remove novelty that fights the page goal, then run design_effect_audit and browser screenshots.

recipes.useWhen: The user asks for glowing text, neon text, text effects, split reveals, or high-impact display type.
recipes.starter: Use one hero-scale glow/shimmer effect; animate reveal with Framer Motion or GSAP split-line timing.

recipes.useWhen: The brief targets $50K-grade design quality, a luxury brand, a premium agency showcase, or any surface where design_luxury_audit must pass.
mustShow: hero headline at clamp(3.5rem, 8vw, 9rem) or larger
font-weight contrast between display (700+) and body (300–400)
custom cubic-bezier easing in :root CSS custom property
staggered entrance: headline delay 0ms, subtext delay 80ms, CTA delay 160ms, visual delay 240ms
at least one bespoke interaction not from a UI kit
avoid: system font in the hero headline
uniform font weights across headline and body
letter-spacing: 0 or positive on display headings
hero body copy longer than 2 lines on first load
recipes.cssStarter: :root { --ease-expo-out: cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); --ease-circ-out: cubic-bezier(0, 0.55, 0.45, 1); } .hero-headline { font-size: clamp(3.5rem, 8vw, 9rem); line-height: 0.95; letter-spacing: -0.03em; font-weight: 900; } .hero-sub { font-size: clamp(1rem, 2vw, 1.375rem); line-height: 1.6; font-weight: 400; } .section { padding-block: clamp(6rem, 12vw, 10rem); } .hero-inner { padding-block: clamp(8rem, 15vw, 14rem); } .content-container { padding-inline: clamp(2rem, 6vw, 6rem); }
recipes.motionStarter: const revealVariants = { hidden: { opacity: 0, y: 24 }, visible: (i) => ({ opacity: 1, y: 0, transition: { delay: i * 0.08, duration: 0.6, ease: [0.16, 1, 0.3, 1] } }) }; // Use custom={0} on headline, custom={1} on subtext, custom={2} on CTA, custom={3} on visual
recipes.scrollStagger: gsap.utils.toArray('.reveal').forEach((el, i) => { gsap.from(el, { scrollTrigger: { trigger: el, start: 'top 85%' }, opacity: 0, y: 32, duration: 0.7, delay: (i % 3) * 0.1, ease: 'expo.out' }); });
